visualReview.notes: Inspected the current whole-model turntable and details. The north château reads through the light walls, dark projecting timber bay, asymmetrical turrets, red-tile ridge and pointed entrance. The red timber residence has two visible storeys and a multiple-hip silhouette. The bridge reads as one continuous enclosed structure at the rear landing and at the companion residence.

sharedSurfaceReview.notes: Inspected nine shared-surface images. Cream lime plaster, red ceramic tiles, red timber and recessed dark glazing remain distinct. Gables and front turrets resolve in the three-quarter view, while the east and west views show the two upper-level bridge connections. Viewer unload passed.

mediumFiReview.notes: Inspected 25 current frames across all four detail levels. Both ends and the straight roofed span persist in every level. The pale and red building masses remain distinct at distance, with balcony balustrades, window framing and the bridge post rhythm visible at closer levels.

geographicReview.notes: The asset uses the mapped château, companion residence and the mapped polygon connecting their rear and front faces. Inspected the original independent 256 m field, the terrain-mounted north view and the side views. The terrain supports both main volumes and the visible bridge piers. The public field resolves the general rise in grade but leaves moat depth and doorstep elevation approximate.

fidelityReview.scope: The standing Chaleemongkolasana and Maleeratanabanlang exteriors at Sanam Chandra Palace and their physically attached upper-floor covered crossing. Includes the north château façade and spired corner towers, red-tile roofs, timber Thai-Western residence and roofed bridge. The separately placed dog monument, shrine and northern halls have independent scopes.
fidelityReview.notes: Ananda’s public-domain original documents the château’s northern face and turrets. The survey describes Maleeratanabanlang as a two-storey, red-painted teak house under red tile and a raised timber connection between upper floors. The companion elevation and bridge fenestration, slopes, pier layout, heights and trim are estimates.

imageryReview.notes: Reviewed 28 published Qualla families first. Qualla’s public-domain château-adjacent hero is Vajariromaya and applies to a different building. The only image used for these connected residences is the matching native château photograph explicitly dedicated to the public domain by the photographer. The companion and bridge use mapped and written evidence.

validation.sharedCaptureScope: The standing Chaleemongkolasana and Maleeratanabanlang residences and their attached covered bridge at Sanam Chandra Palace.

limitations: North château modeling follows the exact Ananda public-domain original. Rear opening spacing, roof heights, turret cross sections and trim motifs are medium-fi estimates.

Maleeratanabanlang uses the named mapped perimeter and the published descriptions of two red teak storeys, rounded arches and timber corridor. Its facade rhythm, hip configuration, bridge glazing and supporting piers are estimated.

The 256 m public source terrain is unchanged. The grade around the moat and elevations of its banks are approximate. The main entrance and companion threshold are independently grounded, and a modest continuous bridge pitch keeps the covered upper-floor passage connected.
Covers the two connected residences and covered crossing. The dog monument, other halls, landscaping and the campus are separate site scopes.
